column90: The following information  should be obtained:  (A) All persons who lived with the case (alive/dead) in the same households since onset of illness.  (b) All persons who visited the patient (alive/dead) either at home or in the health facility since onset of illness.  (c) All places and persons visited by the patient since onset of illness e.g. Hospitals, Clinics, traditional healer, temple, relatives,  etc. All these places and persons should be visited and contacts identified.  (d) All health facilities visited by the patient since onset of illness and all health workers who attended to the patient (alive/dead)  without appropriate infection prevention and control procedures.  (f) During the home visit, the contact tracing/follow-up teams should ask about persons who might have been exposed to the  patient (alive/dead) but were not identified and listed as contacts through the above process. Priority should be given to these  high risk categories of contacts, persons who within the last 14 days:  (a) Touched the patient’s body fluids (blood, vomit, saliva, urine, faeces).  (b) Had direct physical contact with the body of the patient (alive/dead).  (c) Touched or cleaned the linens or clothes of the patient.  (d) Slept or ate in the same household as the patient.  (e) Have been breastfed by the patient (i.e. babies).  (f) Health care workers who suffered a needle-stick injury from a contaminated instrument while attending to a probable or  confirmed Covid-19 patient.  (g) Laboratory workers who had direct contact with specimens collected from suspected Covid-19 without appropriate infection  prevention and control measures.  http://web.archive.org/web/20210607121210/https://health.uk.gov.in/files/Corona/7._Guideline_on_Contact_tracing.pdf

column90: The following information should be obtained for contact tracing:  (A) All persons who lived with the case (alive/dead) in the same households since the onset of illness. column88: ICMR seems to be in the process of focusing testing on individual presenting symptoms of some kind, and generally trying to optimize by not testing individuals in any/all cases:    https://web.archive.org/web/20210505045411/https://www.icmr.gov.in/pdf/covid/strategy/Advisory_COVID_Testing_in_Second_Wave_04052021.pdf    Date: May 4 2021: "Advisory for COVID-19 testing during the second wave of the pandemic"  "RTPCR test must not be repeated in any individual who has tested positive once either by RAT or RTPCR.  No testing is required for COVID-19 recovered individuals at the time of hospital discharge   The need for RTPCR test in healthy individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel may be   completely removed to reduce the load on laboratories. Non-essential travel and interstate travel of symptomatic individuals (COVID-19 or flu like   symptoms) should be essentially avoided to reduce the risk of infection; All asymptomatic individuals undertaking essential travel must follow COVID  appropriate behavior."    "Rapid antigen tests (RATs) were recommended in India for COVID-19 testing in June 2020. However, the   use of these tests is currently limited to containment zones and health care settings."    " Symptomatic individuals identified positive by RAT should not be re-tested and advised   to go through home-based care"    " Symptomatic individuals identified negative by RAT should be linked with RTPCR testfacility  and in the meantime be urged to follow home isolation and treatment.  • All RTPCR and RAT test results should be uploaded on ICMR portal at:  https://cvstatus.icmr.gov.in.  • During the current upsurge of COVID-19 cases, any individual presenting with fever with   / without cough, headache, sore throat, breathlessness, bodyache, recent loss of taste or  smell, fatigue and diarrhea should be considered assuspect case of COVID-19 unless proven   otherwise by confirmation of another etiology."

column88: While the on-ground contact tracing effort in India was always a matter of debate, the official policy of ICMR (Dated May 4 2021) suggests that contact tracing or disease surveillance may be coming under pressure due to the limited testing capacity faced by India -- owing to the sudden and dramatic rise in case counts. Specifically, ICMR seems to be in the process of focusing testing on individual presenting symptoms of some kind, and generally trying to optimize by not testing individuals in any/all cases:    https://web.archive.org/web/20210505045411/https://www.icmr.gov.in/pdf/covid/strategy/Advisory_COVID_Testing_in_Second_Wave_04052021.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20210514161429/https://www.icmr.gov.in/pdf/covid/strategy/Advisory_COVID_Testing_in_Second_Wave_04052021.pdf  Date: May 4 2021: "Advisory for COVID-19 testing during the second wave of the pandemic"  "Rapid antigen tests (RATs) were recommended in India for COVID-19 testing in June 2020. However, the   use of these tests is currently limited to containment zones and health care settings."    "RTPCR test must not be repeated in any individual who has tested positive once either by RAT or RTPCR.  No testing is required for COVID-19 recovered individuals at the time of hospital discharge   The need for RTPCR test in healthy individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel may be   completely removed to reduce the load on laboratories. Non-essential travel and interstate travel of symptomatic individuals (COVID-19 or flu like   symptoms) should be essentially avoided to reduce the risk of infection; All asymptomatic individuals undertaking essential travel must follow COVID  appropriate behavior."

column121: From May 1, 2021, all eligible citizens above the age of 18 years can get the COVID-19 vaccine at vaccination centres run by state governments and private hospitals.     https://web.archive.org/web/20210731095321/https://www.mohfw.gov.in/covid_vaccination/vaccination/faqs.html  http://web.archive.org/web/20210731102121/https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/coronavirus-vaccination-policy-cost-availability-vaccine-explained-7349406/
column129: The Centre will directly procure 50% of the vaccine produced and will be continuing to provide them to States free of cost for administering to priority groups. The State Government and private hospitals have to directly procure from the remaining 50% vaccine pool. Healthcare workers, frontline workers and those above 45 will continue to be vaccinated for FREE at the vaccination centres run by the central government, while every citizen above the age of 18 will be vaccinated FREE at vaccination centres run by state government.     People of all ages will have to pay for vaccination at private centres (at a maximum service charge of Rs 150 over and above the price of the vaccine). Thus, individuals and beneficiaries of the hospitals must pay a fee for the vaccine. General age groups have been marked as 'partially funded by the government' to reflect this reality.     http://web.archive.org/web/20210731091030/https://www.mohfw.gov.in/pdf/RevisedVaccinationGuidelines.pdf  http://web.archive.org/web/20210731102121/https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/coronavirus-vaccination-policy-cost-availability-vaccine-explained-7349406/

column121: From June 21, 2021, all eligible citizens above the age of 18 years can now get the COVID-19 vaccine at centre government run vaccination centres in addition to the vaccination centres run by state governments and private hospitals.     Note: Healthcare workers and frontline workers will continue to get top priority at government centres. Depending on potential supply, states will also have to prioritise the vaccination of citizens above 45 since this category accounts for 80% of Covid-related mortality. They will also have to prioritise the vaccination of those whose second dose has become due, the revised policy guidelines recommend. Within the population group of citizens in the 18-44 age group, states may decide their own prioritisation factoring in the vaccine supply schedule.    https://web.archive.org/web/20210731095321/https://www.mohfw.gov.in/covid_vaccination/vaccination/faqs.html  http://web.archive.org/web/20210731102121/https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/coronavirus-vaccination-policy-cost-availability-vaccine-explained-7349406/  http://web.archive.org/web/20210731091030/https://www.mohfw.gov.in/pdf/RevisedVaccinationGuidelines.pdf
column129: The Centre will directly procure 75% of the doses manufactured by vaccine companies, and distribute this among the states, to be administered free (from June 21, states will no longer have any role in procurement). Healthcare workers and frontline workers will continue to get top priority at government centres and will be vaccinated for FREE, and starting from June 21, every citizen above the age of 18 will also be vaccinated FREE at vaccination centres run by the Centre or a state government.     Private hospitals will have exclusive access to the remaining 25%, and people of all ages will have to pay for vaccination at private centres (at a maximum service charge of Rs 150 over and above the price of the vaccine). Thus, individuals and beneficiaries of the hospitals must pay a fee for the vaccine. General age groups have been marked as 'partially funded by the government' to reflect this reality.     http://web.archive.org/web/20210731091030/https://www.mohfw.gov.in/pdf/RevisedVaccinationGuidelines.pdf  http://web.archive.org/web/20210731102121/https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/coronavirus-vaccination-policy-cost-availability-vaccine-explained-7349406/
